piezas.titular: Let’s keep virtual reality headsets for tasks where the point of view matters
piezas.entradilla: To draw a cove, a map may be enough. To work out at which bend in the path the lighthouse drops out of sight, it does make sense to step into the landscape.
cuerpo: Suppose a geography class has to work out where the lighthouse of a cove can be seen from. On a map, two points on the coast look equally good. With virtual reality headsets, each pair could stand at both points, look towards the lighthouse and discover that from one of them the cliff blocks the view. If I were defending headsets in the classroom, I would start there. There is something worth doing inside that scene.

There is also a reason why teachers might want to build it with the help of artificial intelligence. They may be interested precisely in the cove the group knows, with the path they walk and the bend beyond which the lighthouse disappears. A virtual stroll along a spectacular coast picked from a catalogue would be of little use in settling that question. Being able to choose the place and decide where to stop justifies the work of preparing your own material, as long as someone then checks on a map or on the ground that the generated relief matches the real place.

Let’s change the question without leaving the cove. If the task is to draw its outline and mark where it opens to the sea, I would leave the headsets in the cupboard. I would put a map on the table so that two students could follow the same line with a finger and argue about where the cove ends. I would reserve the headset for tasks in which looking from somewhere else solves a specific difficulty.

Enthusiasm counts too. As part of a [project funded by Spain’s Ministry of Science and Innovation](https://investigacion.us.es/sisius/sis_proyecto.php?idproy=37676), researchers from the universities of Seville and Granada compared the motivation of 217 education sciences students working with headsets and on a screen. They found very similar effects in both formats, with somewhat more engagement and enthusiasm in the immersive one, according to their [study on motivation and virtual reality](https://revistas.um.es/red/article/view/707221). I would give that enthusiasm a value of its own. If it awakens a desire to travel along a coast or to find out what lies on the other side, we already have a way to start the lesson.

Another study, co-authored by Julio Cabero Almenara, one of the leaders of that project, randomly assigned 336 university education students to either a headset version or one on a computer screen. Both groups improved between the pre-test and the post-test, and the screen group got better results, with moderate effect sizes, according to the [article by the research team](https://revistas.uautonoma.cl/index.php/ejep/article/view/3416). What was measured matters. According to its abstract, performance was assessed with objective knowledge tests, and there is no sign that spatial orientation was measured. To find out whether headsets help with orientation, the group would have to be given the chance to find its way.

To prepare the cove session I would start with a sheet of paper, even in a school that already had headsets. I would make a fold to represent the cliff and stand a pencil behind it as the lighthouse. A pair could look at the table from above, mark the spot from which they think they will see the tip, and lower their eyes to the mark to check. When the pencil is moved, they would have to choose another spot and explain their choice. If that change of height is enough to understand the problem, I would spend the rest of the session reading the map.

When would I take the next step? When the group understood the paper example and still could not recognise on the map the hillock that cuts off the view as they walk. The paper reported on [how to turn a real map into a relief model](pieza:2026-11-12/relleu-obert). With a model, the view from above could be rehearsed. If we also had a headset version, I would use it to walk the path at eye level. Before putting on the headset, each pair would mark on the map the last point from which they expect to see the lighthouse. The walk would stop there so that they could compare what they had drawn with what is in front of them.

repaso: Párrafo 4: “investigadoras” pasa a “investigadores” (no consta el género) y “respuestas parecidas” a “efectos muy parecidos… implicación y entusiasmo”, como dice el estudio.

Párrafo 5: quitadas las afirmaciones que no se pudieron comprobar (visita a un aula, 25 preguntas de elección múltiple, “pequeña ventaja”); ahora dice lo que consta en el resumen (336 estudiantes universitarios de Educación, reparto al azar, ambos mejoran, mejores resultados en pantalla con efectos moderados, pruebas objetivas de conocimientos). El vínculo con el proyecto se atribuye a la autoría (Cabero Almenara figura como responsable del proyecto), no a una financiación que no consta. El enlace pasa del PDF de IDUS (403, no verificable) a la página de la revista.
Fuentes: sustituida la dirección del tercer estudio por la de la revista.
Aviso sobre la nota (no se ha tocado): #15025 preguntó por visores en una simulación 3D compartida, no en un “laboratorio virtual”.
piezas.comprobado: Proyecto MEREVIA (investigacion.us.es): financiado por el Ministerio de Ciencia e Innovación, Plan Estatal 2021-2023, 2023-2027, responsables Llorente Cejudo y Cabero Almenara. Estudio de motivación (revistas.um.es): 217 estudiantes de Ciencias de la Educación de la Universidad de Sevilla, autoría de Sevilla y Granada, efectos muy parecidos con algo más de implicación y entusiasmo en la inmersiva, 1-7-2026, cita el proyecto. Estudio de rendimiento (revistas.uautonoma.cl, resumen): 336 estudiantes de Educación, reparto aleatorio, preprueba y posprueba, ambos mejoran, mejor el grupo de escritorio con efectos moderados, pruebas objetivas; el texto completo no se pudo abrir, por eso se quitan los detalles que solo estaban en él. Mensajes #15025, #15027, #15028, #12275, #12280, #12281, #14965 y #14966 contra el material: recogen el debate sin identificar a nadie. Enlace pieza:2026-11-12/relleu-obert, en la lista de lo publicado y sobre la maqueta 3D de relieve. Ejemplos de la cala, el faro y el folio, presentados como hipótesis. Sin “quien/quienes”. Cuerpo de unas 650 palabras; titular de 90 caracteres.
